View in browser             Sponsored by       Dawn Gilbertson   Southwest, United Shake Up Their Frequent-Flier Programs   Plus, Delta gussies up business class, and there’s a new terminal at L.A.’s easiest airport   Happy Friday. I traveled to New York, Dallas and back since last week’s newsletter.  

   It was a big week for frequent-flier program changes, with Southwest and United shaking things up. More on that below. 

   Southwest was in the spotlight for other news, too. The airline unveiled the name of the new airport lounges it is developing with Chase. Drum roll, please: Icon Lounge. If you don’t think that sounds much like typically spunky Southwest, you’re right. The airline’s execs say it nods to Southwest’s iconic history and founder Herb Kelleher, an industry icon. 

   The first one is expected to open late next year in Nashville. Southwest didn’t spill any more details on the new premium Chase credit card that will get you in, but look for it sometime next year. And bet on the annual fee being much higher than Southwest’s current priciest card ($229 for the Southwest Priority card). 

   Delta Air Lines has led the U.S. airline industry’s premium-travel push and this week we got a look at what’s coming to its pricey Delta One business-class cabin. Look for new suites with plush padding, longer lie-flat beds and nifty touches like a hook for your glasses, plus a revamped food and alcohol menu. I tried the sea bass and give it a 10/10. Let’s hope it translates at 35,000 feet. 

   In Southern California, Hollywood Burbank Airport opened its long-awaited new terminal . If you’ve never flown out of there, it’s a dream compared with LAX.  

   And more bad news on airfares in September’s inflation report . They were up 22% from a year earlier. 

       Frequent-flier changes     KEVIN CARTER/GETTY IMAGES   If you’re loyal to United or Southwest, get ready for some major frequent-flier changes. It’s no shock that spending and airline credit cards play an increasingly bigger role in earning status.

   United is taking away the option to reach Premier status with a combination of flights and spending. Beginning Jan. 1, it’s all about Premier qualifying points . The airline says it’s simplifying the program. Here’s one United frequent flier’s hot take . 

   United is also raising the amount of money you need to spend to reach its highest public status, 1K.

   Southwest, meanwhile, is completely overhauling its Rapid Rewards program given the airline’s dramatic changes over the past 18 months.

   Today it has two major tiers: A List and A List Preferred. They require 20 or 40 one-way flights a year, respectively, or set spending levels. (I have A List.)

   Beginning in January, those names are gone. Southwest will now have silver, gold and platinum status. A List becomes silver, A List Preferred, gold. Platinum is new and effectively replaces its current Companion Pass program. You can earn any level through flights or spending. If you do it on flights, which I do, the number of flights for silver is going up from 20 to 25.

   If those gem names sound like every other airline’s tiers, you’re right. My predecessor, longtime Middle Seat columnist Scott McCartney, asked Southwest executives why they didn’t get more creative like the Southwest of old. His cheeky suggestion: Herb (Kelleher), Gary (Kelly) and Colleen (Barrett) tiers. Kelly was the airline’s longtime CEO, Colleen a longtime top executive credited with the airline’s culture.

   Tony Roach, Southwest’s chief customer and brand officer, said Southwest debated names at length but kept it simple because that’s what frequent travelers know best.

   • A hip replacement didn’t sideline this mother-son duo. They tested the new hip on an Iceland adventure .

   • A roller coaster death casts a shadow on Six Flags’ turnaround hopes .

Every villa across Sicily, Puglia, Tuscany, Sardinia, Greece and Corsica is personally chosen and paired with a specialist who knows it firsthand. Named World’s Best Villa Rental Company 10 times by Condé Nast Traveller readers. Speak with a specialist now.   Learn More  >       One Good Tip 🎯   Want to know if your next United flight will have speedy Wi-Fi? Check out the airline’s new Starlink tracker . You can check within three days of departure and it even accounts for last-minute plane swaps, the airline says. Starlink, which United says is now on nearly half of its planes, can’t come soon enough to its long-haul flights .

       Travel Math 🧮   $16   The cost to get from JFK to Midtown Manhattan this week. How? I took the AirTrain to Jamaica Station, hopped on a Long Island Rail Road train to Grand Central Station and walked less than a mile to my hotel in Midtown Manhattan. It would be a slog with a lot of bags or in wintry weather, but it was perfect. The going price for an Uber when I landed midafternoon: $165.

       And We Quote 💬   “We’re not trying to become those carriers at all. But if that is what consumers want, then Southwest Airlines will not be left out.”

   — Southwest CEO Bob Jordan, on chatter that the airline plans to add wide-body jets to its fleet to serve more international destinations. American, Delta and United already do that, of course. 

       You Have Thoughts 🤔   …on the ups and downs of renting an electric vehicle :  

   • “Big mistake, Dawn. If you had rented a Tesla, there would have been two huge benefits. One, you enter your destination in on the app, then the car stops and parks at each charging station needed along the way, with no further input by you. Second, for a few extra dollars you can have full self-driving (FSD) activated and enjoy the ride stress-free. We just returned from Hawaii where we rented a Tesla and if it works in Hawaii, it works anywhere. We bought two Teslas upon our return.” — Roy Farrow, Nevada  

   • “I think a better title is, ‘Like an idiot, without any preparation, I got involved with a technology I had never used. It was new, and I got really nervous as I used it. And in the end everything worked out.’” — Neal Hogan, New Hampshire 

   …on airport-line cutting options : 

   • “Just a quick mahalo for the mention of this perk. Signed up immediately after reading the article. Last time through Las Vegas I peeked over from the PreCheck line (10 people) and noticed Touchless had only a single person. Every minute counts, I guess.” — Timothy Tynan, California  

   …on in-flight Zoom meetings : 

   • “If someone boots up a Zoom or Teams meeting on my flight, I take that as an invitation to join the call and share my political predictions for the midterms!” — Craig Nelson, California 

   (Responses have been condensed and edited.) 

       Cheers and Jeers 🤷   Cheers to no waits at the side-by-side Chase Sapphire and American Express Centurion lounges at the dreamy Terminal B at New York’s LaGuardia Airport on Wednesday. It was my first visit to both.

   Cheers, too, to the Delta flight attendants who passed through with the Comfort Plus snack basket twice on a cross-country flight. You can never have enough snacks in your backpack on the road.

   Jeers to the Dream Midtown hotel in Manhattan. The Wi-Fi was out two mornings in a row. One time I called, the agent said she notified IT but it was early so she didn’t know when it would be back on. It was 7 a.m.!

Southwest, United Shake Up Their Frequent-Flier Programs
 
Plus, Delta gussies up business class, and there’s a new terminal at L.A.’s easiest airport
 

Happy Friday. I traveled to New York, Dallas and back since last week’s newsletter. 

 

It was a big week for frequent-flier program changes, with Southwest and United shaking things up. More on that below.

 

Southwest was in the spotlight for other news, too. The airline unveiled the name of the new airport lounges it is developing with Chase. Drum roll, please: Icon Lounge. If you don’t think that sounds much like typically spunky Southwest, you’re right. The airline’s execs say it nods to Southwest’s iconic history and founder Herb Kelleher, an industry icon.

And more bad news on airfares in September’s inflation report. They were up 22% from a year earlier.

 
 
 

Frequent-flier changes

 
 
KEVIN CARTER/GETTY IMAGES
 

If you’re loyal to United or Southwest, get ready for some major frequent-flier changes. It’s no shock that spending and airline credit cards play an increasingly bigger role in earning status.

 

United is taking away the option to reach Premier status with a combination of flights and spending. Beginning Jan. 1, it’s all about Premier qualifying points. The airline says it’s simplifying the program. Here’s one United frequent flier’s hot take. 

 

United is also raising the amount of money you need to spend to reach its highest public status, 1K.

 

Southwest, meanwhile, is completely overhauling its Rapid Rewards program given the airline’s dramatic changes over the past 18 months.

 

Today it has two major tiers: A List and A List Preferred. They require 20 or 40 one-way flights a year, respectively, or set spending levels. (I have A List.)

 

Beginning in January, those names are gone. Southwest will now have silver, gold and platinum status. A List becomes silver, A List Preferred, gold. Platinum is new and effectively replaces its current Companion Pass program. You can earn any level through flights or spending. If you do it on flights, which I do, the number of flights for silver is going up from 20 to 25.

 

If those gem names sound like every other airline’s tiers, you’re right. My predecessor, longtime Middle Seat columnist Scott McCartney, asked Southwest executives why they didn’t get more creative like the Southwest of old. His cheeky suggestion: Herb (Kelleher), Gary (Kelly) and Colleen (Barrett) tiers. Kelly was the airline’s longtime CEO, Colleen a longtime top executive credited with the airline’s culture.

 

Tony Roach, Southwest’s chief customer and brand officer, said Southwest debated names at length but kept it simple because that’s what frequent travelers know best.

One Good Tip 🎯

 

Want to know if your next United flight will have speedy Wi-Fi? Check out the airline’s new Starlink tracker. You can check within three days of departure and it even accounts for last-minute plane swaps, the airline says. Starlink, which United says is now on nearly half of its planes, can’t come soon enough to its long-haul flights.

 
 
 

Travel Math 🧮

 
$16
 

The cost to get from JFK to Midtown Manhattan this week. How? I took the AirTrain to Jamaica Station, hopped on a Long Island Rail Road train to Grand Central Station and walked less than a mile to my hotel in Midtown Manhattan. It would be a slog with a lot of bags or in wintry weather, but it was perfect. The going price for an Uber when I landed midafternoon: $165.

 
 
 

And We Quote 💬

 

“We’re not trying to become those carriers at all. But if that is what consumers want, then Southwest Airlines will not be left out.”

 

— Southwest CEO Bob Jordan, on chatter that the airline plans to add wide-body jets to its fleet to serve more international destinations. American, Delta and United already do that, of course. 

 
 
 

You Have Thoughts 🤔

 

…on the ups and downs of renting an electric vehicle: 

 

• “Big mistake, Dawn. If you had rented a Tesla, there would have been two huge benefits. One, you enter your destination in on the app, then the car stops and parks at each charging station needed along the way, with no further input by you. Second, for a few extra dollars you can have full self-driving (FSD) activated and enjoy the ride stress-free. We just returned from Hawaii where we rented a Tesla and if it works in Hawaii, it works anywhere. We bought two Teslas upon our return.” —Roy Farrow, Nevada 

 

• “I think a better title is, ‘Like an idiot, without any preparation, I got involved with a technology I had never used. It was new, and I got really nervous as I used it. And in the end everything worked out.’” —Neal Hogan, New Hampshire

• “Just a quick mahalo for the mention of this perk. Signed up immediately after reading the article. Last time through Las Vegas I peeked over from the PreCheck line (10 people) and noticed Touchless had only a single person. Every minute counts, I guess.” —Timothy Tynan, California 

 

…on in-flight Zoom meetings:

 

• “If someone boots up a Zoom or Teams meeting on my flight, I take that as an invitation to join the call and share my political predictions for the midterms!” —Craig Nelson, California

 

(Responses have been condensed and edited.)

 
 
 

Cheers and Jeers 🤷

 

Cheers to no waits at the side-by-side Chase Sapphire and American Express Centurion lounges at the dreamy Terminal B at New York’s LaGuardia Airport on Wednesday. It was my first visit to both.

 

Cheers, too, to the Delta flight attendants who passed through with the Comfort Plus snack basket twice on a cross-country flight. You can never have enough snacks in your backpack on the road.
